findings.evidence: "This is simply how patron behavior works, and no library that has tried it has ever found otherwise." (line 27) is the section's only content bearing on the systemwide claim; the preceding sentence (line 25) is about updating the catalog's fine-display field and does not speak to generalization at all.
findings.fix: Cite evidence that fine elimination's effects generalize beyond a partial pilot (comparable rollouts at other consortia, or data showing the five non-pilot branches resemble the pilot branches), or qualify the recommendation to flag that systemwide generalization is extrapolated rather than demonstrated.
findings.location: the "Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide" section, lines 23-27
findings.violation: The principle that licenses extending the pilot's 5-branch, 18-month result to a permanent, systemwide policy across all ten branches and every item type is asserted as universally and unfalsifiably true ('no library ... has ever found otherwise') rather than supported with a study, a comparison to other library systems, or data about the five non-pilot branches. The target reader, who grants only what is supplied, would not accept this sweeping generalization on sight, and the artifact offers nothing beyond restating it forcefully.

findings.evidence: Line 31 states the objection: "A skeptic on the board points to overdue fines as a source of materials-replacement funding, and argues that eliminating them systemwide will leave a shortfall the consortium has not planned for." The section's only further sentence (line 33) is "The branch renovation project remains on schedule for completion next spring."
findings.fix: Replace the renovation-project sentence with an actual answer to the revenue concern: a replacement funding source, a projected shortfall estimate, or a stated reason the shortfall is acceptable or will be offset.
findings.location: the "Addressing the Revenue Concern" section, lines 29-33
findings.violation: The artifact raises the one objection its own recommendation most directly exposes - loss of materials-replacement revenue from eliminating fines consortium-wide - then moves on to an unrelated fact about a renovation project's schedule without answering it, leaving the funding shortfall the skeptic names completely unaddressed.

findings.evidence: "This recommendation applies to items returned within 60 days of their due date; items still unreturned past that window remain subject to the existing replacement-cost billing process, matching the return-rate pattern the pilot data actually established."
findings.fix: Report the pilot's own return-timing breakdown (for example, what share of 'eventual' returns came back within 60 days versus later) so the 60-day threshold is traceable to a stated figure, or drop the claim that it matches the pilot data if that breakdown was never collected.
findings.violation: The claim that a 60-day cutoff 'match[es] the return-rate pattern the pilot data actually established' asserts a specific finding the pilot description never reports: "What the Pilot Showed" gives only an aggregate 93%-vs-86% return rate and a survey result, with no breakdown of returns by elapsed time. A reader has no evidence to check that 60 days is the point the pilot data actually supports rather than a figure asserted to be grounded without being shown.
